title: Session 1 — Participant 48 User + Claude Behavior Graph
goal: Identify and biologically interpret differentially expressed genes between two experimental conditions using a prepared RNA-seq count dataset, and produce a concise summary of the main findings with appropriate visualizations.
context: I am choosing a bioinformatics goal because my professional work involves analyzing biological datasets to identify meaningful patterns and generate evidence-based biological conclusions. In this session, I will work with an RNA-seq dataset, which measures the activity of thousands of genes across different biological samples. The purpose of the workflow is to compare two experimental conditions, determine which genes show meaningful differences in activity, and interpret what those differences may indicate biologically. The workflow involves checking the dataset and experimental design, assessing data quality, performing statistical analysis, visualizing results, and interpreting the findings. This is suitable for the study because it involves several connected analytical and decision-making steps rather than a single repetitive task.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: Yes, I was able to analyse the data and it gave me the main findings.

Step 1.step_name: Load and inspect the RNA-seq dataset
Step 1.step_action: I will load the RNA-seq count matrix and sample metadata into R and inspect their basic structure. I will check the number of genes and samples, confirm the files load correctly, and identify obvious formatting or missing-data issues. I will use Claude if I need help understanding the structure of the files or troubleshooting import problems.

nodes.label: Ask Claude Code to navigate to the dataset folder and check the exist data
nodes.detail: Types 'go to desktop folder named RNAseq_mus' into the Claude Code CLI terminal (Windows).

nodes.label: Navigate to folder and list its contents
nodes.detail: No folder exists named exactly 'RNAseq_mus', so Claude lists similar candidates (RNA_mus, RNA-seq, RNA-seq_kidney) and asks which one is meant; the participant answers RNA_mus. Claude confirms the correct folder (Desktop\RNA_mus) and lists its contents: a metadata file (GSE215113_metadata.tsv) and 6 STAR ReadsPerGene.out.tab count files. The participant then clears the terminal and asks it to show the file names again, and Claude lists all 6 files by their full GSM IDs (3 GSM6622152-154 OO_Control / C75S mutant, 3 GSM6622155-157 WT_control replicates).

nodes.label: Issue combined load/match/persist-script instruction
nodes.detail: Narrates aloud that this is an RNA-seq differential expression analysis on a mouse dataset, then types (over several minutes) a single combined instruction: load R, read all 6 count files and the metadata file, match sample information from metadata to the actual file names, and create/save a persistent analysis script updated throughout the session.

nodes.label: Write and Run RNAseq_mus_analysis.R to Load and Match Data
nodes.detail: Discovers R 4.6.0 is installed but not on PATH and works around it by calling Rscript with its full path; writes a 123-line script that reads all 6 count files, builds a 55,487 gene × 6 sample raw count matrix, and constructs colData capturing sample_id, condition (WT vs C75S, 3 reps each), and replicate. Runs the script, confirms successful data load and matching — samples correctly ordered and named, strandedness auto-detected as unstranded — and saves counts_matrix.rds, coldata.rds, and rnaseq_mus_loaded.RData to disk for reuse.

nodes.label: Review the loaded data
nodes.detail: Reviews Claude's confirmation that the six count files and metadata were loaded successfully, verifies that the sample IDs match the metadata and checks the sample condition information before proceeding to the next analysis step.

Step 2.step_name: Assess sample quality and confirm the experimental design
Step 2.step_action: I will check whether the biological samples behave as expected and confirm that the experimental groups are represented correctly. I will examine sample labels, experimental conditions, biological replicates, library sizes, and sample relationships using exploratory analyses such as PCA or sample-distance plots. I will use Claude to help interpret unexpected clustering, possible outliers, or inconsistencies in the experimental design.

nodes.label: Instruct Claude to run full QC pipeline with an explicit hold on DGE
nodes.detail: Types a long, detailed instruction (visibly composed over several minutes): calculate/inspect library sizes, build a DESeq2 dataset with design=condition, remove only extremely low-count genes with a clearly stated rule, apply VST for exploratory analysis, generate a library-size chart and a PCA plot, explain whether samples cluster by condition, identify potential outliers, and explicitly not remove any sample or run DGE without approval.

nodes.label: Extend Script with Filtering, VST, PCA, and Heatmap Code; Deliver QC Summary
nodes.detail: Extends the master R script to filter low-count genes (55,487 → 13,046 genes kept, requiring count ≥ 10 in at least 3 samples), relevels the condition factor, computes VST, and generates a PCA plot and sample-to-sample distance heatmap. Runs the full script as a background Rscript process (~2 minutes). Reports library sizes ranging 16.7M–20.7M reads per sample with no severe outliers, 76.5% of genes removed by filtering, and PCA (PC1 = 62% variance) cleanly separating WT from C75S — while flagging GSM6622154 (C75S rep3) for elevated within-group dispersion on PC2 relative to its replicates, though it does not cross condition lines. Concludes data is suitable for DE testing with no samples removed.

nodes.label: Open png to visually inspect clustering
nodes.detail: Opens the saved library_ sizes.png and pca_plot.png directly from qc_plots in the Windows Photos viewer and visually confirms PC1 (62% variance) separates WT (red, GSM6622155-157) from C75S (teal, GSM6622152-154), with GSM6622154 sitting noticeably lower on PC2 (near -3) than its two replicates.

Step 3.step_action: I will use DESeq2 to statistically compare gene expression between the two experimental conditions. I will define the appropriate design and contrast, run the differential expression analysis, and identify genes using adjusted p-value and effect-size criteria. I will use Claude to review the analysis code, help explain statistical outputs, and identify possible errors or inappropriate assumptions.

nodes.label: Request DESeq2 run with explicit design/contrast and thresholds
nodes.detail: Instructs Claude to show the exact DESeq2 design and contrast before running, then run WT vs C75S differential expression using adjusted p-value < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 1 as significance criteria, and save results tables and a significant-genes table plus a report.

nodes.label: Run DESeq2 Pipeline in Background Script; Deliver DGE Results Summary and Biological Interpretation
nodes.detail: Extends the master script with the DESeq2 fit, contrast, and results extraction, then executes it as a background Rscript process against the filtered, VST-QC'd dataset from Step 2. Reports 13,046 total genes tested (non-NA padj), 381 genes with padj < 0.05, and a final significant set of 24 genes meeting both thresholds (6 upregulated in WT, 18 downregulated in WT / upregulated in C75S). Flags outlier gene ENSMUSG00000039323 (log2FC = −1.76, padj ≈ 1.0×10⁻⁹) and independently looks up GEO accession GSE215113 to identify the study as an AEG-1 (Metadherin/MTDH) Cys75Ser palmitoylation-site knock-in study in mouse hepatocytes — interpreting the modest 24-gene signature as consistent with a single point mutation rather than a full knockout. Saves DGE_WT_vs_C75S_all_results.csv, DGE_WT_vs_C75S_significant.csv, and an initial volcano_plot.png.

nodes.label: Review DGE summary and briefly check email during background run
nodes.detail: Reads through the DGE results table and outlier-gene flag; during the earlier background run switches briefly (well under a minute, around the 24-minute mark) to a Gmail/Upwork browser tab before returning to the terminal to continue the analysis.
nodes.softwares: Claude Code (CLI terminal), Gmail (brief incidental check)

Step 4.step_name: Visualize the results and investigate biological functions
Step 4.step_action: I will create visualizations such as a volcano plot, MA plot, or heatmap to examine the major patterns in the differential expression results. I will then use the significant gene list for functional annotation or pathway-enrichment analysis to identify biological processes associated with the observed expression changes. I will use Claude to help interpret visual patterns and evaluate the biological relevance of enriched functions or pathways.

nodes.label: Issue combined plotting + enrichment instruction
nodes.detail: In one long instruction (composed over several minutes), asks Claude to generate high-quality labeled MA and volcano plots (labeling only the small number of highly differentially expressed genes), summarize the strongest visual pattern, then run functional enrichment on the significant genes -- explicitly requiring it to double-check the organism (Mus musculus), use an appropriate annotation package and gene-ID conversion method, run GO/KEGG analysis, and separate results directly supported by the analysis from possible biological interpretation.

nodes.label: Install Annotation Package, Run Full Visualization and Enrichment Pipeline, and Deliver Final Results
nodes.detail: Installs the missing org.Mm.eg.db mouse annotation package (clusterProfiler and enrichplot already available), then extends the master script with MA plot, volcano plot, and GO/KEGG enrichment sections. Executes the full pipeline end-to-end as a long-running background task (~20 min 40 sec), mapping Ensembl IDs to Entrez/Symbol via AnnotationDbi::mapIds (93.9% of tested genes mapped, 22/24 significant genes mapped), through several rounds of scratchpad-tested code fixes and at least one full re-run. GO enrichment finds 6 of 538 terms significant at FDR < 0.05 — a keratin/cornified-envelope cluster driven by Krt17, Krt20, and Ivl — and KEGG enrichment finds 2 of 31 pathways significant (cornified envelope formation and S. aureus infection, driven by the same keratin genes). Delivers labeled MA and volcano plots (top 10 genes labeled by symbol, Igfbp2 as the dominant outlier by padj), GO/KEGG dotplots, and a written Functional_Enrichment_Report.md. Explicitly separates directly-supported findings (each enriched term driven by only 2–3 genes) from flagged speculative interpretation (the keratin signature being unusual for hepatocytes — potentially real AEG-1-driven biology or a technical/isolation artifact).
nodes.softwares: Claude Code (CLI terminal), R, org.Mm.eg.db, clusterProfiler

nodes.label: Review the enrichment results
nodes.detail: Reviews the completed visualization and functional-enrichment outputs, including the labeled significant genes, GO terms, significant pathways, and detailed report, and confirms that the results look fine before requesting a comprehensive scientific report.

Step 5.step_name: Summarize and critically evaluate the biological findings and write a short report
Step 5.step_action: I will combine the quality-control results, differential expression findings, visualizations, and functional analysis into a concise interpretation of the experiment. I will identify the strongest conclusions supported by the data, distinguish those conclusions from more speculative hypotheses, and note important limitations or uncertainties. I will use Claude as a critical reviewer to identify possible overinterpretation and help refine the final scientific summary.

nodes.label: Request full scientific report with built-in fact-check requirement
nodes.detail: In a single detailed instruction (composed over several minutes), asks Claude to write a scientific report structured into methods, results, biological interpretation, limitations, and conclusion, explicitly instructing it not to invent genes, statistics, mechanisms, or biological facts, to summarize QC/significant genes/pathways with figure references, to clearly distinguish direct evidence from interpretation in the biological-interpretation section, and to identify important limitations and anything requiring additional validation.

nodes.label: Write the first draft scientific report
nodes.detail: Writes a 288-line Scientific_Report_WT_vs_C75S.md covering the AEG-1 C75S palmitoylation-site study, QC summary, the 24 significant genes, GO/KEGG enrichment results, and limitations; explains its key design choices (every number pulled from the pipeline's own CSVs/objects, GEO metadata facts sourced from the fetched GSE215113 record, no AEG-1-specific pathway mechanism asserted since unverified within this session).

nodes.label: Request PDF conversion plus an explicit second critical-audit pass
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to generate a nicer PDF, but first to double-check everything in the report for unsupported claims, over-interpretation, numerical inconsistencies against the underlying data, and any missed limitations, and to ensure the conclusion is concise and evidence-based.

nodes.label: Self-Audit Report Claims, Correct Three Real Issues, and Convert to Polished PDF
nodes.detail: Re-verifies every claim in the draft report against the actual pipeline output files (numerically checking the sample-distance matrix and KEGG enrichment CSV rather than relying on memory or visual inspection), then finds and corrects three real issues: (1) a factual overclaim that PI3K-Akt signaling showed "nominal significance" when its actual values (p = 0.063, padj = 0.177) did not clear even the p < 0.05 threshold — replaced with exact p-values for pathways that genuinely came close (Estrogen signaling p = 0.009/padj = 0.096, Cadherin signaling p = 0.047/padj = 0.177, both non-significant after FDR correction and both driven by the same two keratin genes); (2) an overstated claim that the sample-distance heatmap "corroborated" the PCA outlier signal for GSM6622154 — corrected to note that only one of its two pairwise distances exceeds baseline, making the effect PCA/top-variance-gene-specific rather than a whole-transcriptome signal; (3) a missing finding that all 8 significant GO/KEGG hits (6 GO terms + 2 KEGG pathways) trace back to only 5 unique genes (Krt17, Krt20, Ivl, Rbp1, Ptgds), added as both a results fact and an explicit limitation. Also adds missing limitations covering absent batch/RIN metadata, reliance on empirical-Bayes shrinkage dispersion estimation at n = 3, lack of independent experimental validation, raw non-shrunken log2FC estimates, hard significance thresholds vs. rank-based alternatives, and a 48-hour post-isolation confound; tightens the conclusion to remove an unsupported "reproducible" claim. Builds a print-ready HTML version and converts it to PDF via headless Chrome (Scientific_Report_WT_vs_C75S.pdf, ~648 KB with 7 embedded figures and tables).

nodes.label: Confirm the final report is complete
nodes.detail: Confirms that the requested scientific report and final PDF have been generated and that the requested analysis and reporting task is complete.
